MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, FEBRUARY 1, 2021

  A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
  order by CHAIR CARMAN at 7:00 p.m. Pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20, this
  meeting was held via teleconference.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR CARMAN led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Carman, Edler, Medawar, Schachter, Scott, Yoo, Zigrang

  Staff Members Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Planning Manager
  Kelley Thom, Associate Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  Item 5A taken out of order.

  5.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES, DECEMBER 7, 2020.

  CHAIR CARMAN noted a typo in Item 7B.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  APPROVE THE AMENDED PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF
  DECEMBER 7, 2020.

  There being no objection, CHAIR CARMAN so ordered.

  4. PLANNING COMMISSION REORGANIZATION

  Planning Manager Naughton thanked CHAIR CARMAN for her service as the Planning Commission
  Chair for year 2020-2021 and presented her with a plaque on behalf of the City.

  At their meeting of January 26, 2021, the City Council appointed VICE CHAIR EDLER as CHAIR of
  the PLANNING COMMISSION and COMMISSIONER SCOTT as VICE CHAIR of the PLANNING
  COMMISSION.

  6. AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

  7.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  NONE

  8.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-200221; ADDRESS: 91 DAPPLEGRAY LANE,
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES; APPLICANT: KRISTI SKELTON, UNBOUND
  ARCHITECTURE; A request for approval of a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination
  (NC-200222) for a 200 sq. ft. extension of an existing second story deck over a one-story
  357 sq. ft. addition.

  ASSOCIATE PLANNER THOM presented Planning Application No. PA-200221 and stated that
  this item was continued to allow the applicant and the neighbor, at 87 Dapplegray Lane, to address
  privacy concerns. The privacy concern was due to a window in the laundry room of the lower level.
  The applicant has agreed to install opaque glass in the window and a hedge will be planted in
  between the two properties.

  ASSOCIATE PLANNER THOM stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission
  approval Planning Application No. PA-200221 with the conditions noted in the staff report.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT asked for clarification on the section of the staff report pertaining to the legally
  conforming attached garage, which will be rebuilt under a separate approval. Associate Planner

MINUTES, FEBRUARY 1, 2021
   Thom stated that the rebuilt of the garage (Phase 1) was approved prior to this application and did
  not require any entitlements; the garage rebuild was an over-the-counter approval.

  KRISTI SKELTON, UNBOUND ARCHITECTURE, stated that Phase 1 was due subsidence. The
  entire front of the house is being underpinned. Ms. Skelton stated that the property owner and
  neighbor were able to resolve the privacy issues in a very friendly manner.

  VICE CHAIR SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER CARMAN to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-200369 as presented.

  Ayes: Carman, Edler, Medawar, Schachter, Scott, Yoo, Zigrang
  Noes:
  Absent:
  Abstain:

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Planning
  Application No. PA-200221. There is a 20-day appeal period for this item where any member of
  the public may appeal the decision to the City Council.

  9.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  NONE

  10.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  Per a request from VICE CHAIR SCOTT, Planning Manager Naughton provided an update on 9
  Lantana and stated that staff is working directly with the architect and property owner to get through
  the building plan check process. There were two actions that affect this property, the first is Assembly
  Bill (AB) 1561 that went into effect January 1st and extends city housing entitlements, including
  building permits that were in effect in March 2020 and would expire at the end of 2021; AB 1561
  allows an additional eighteen month extension due to the COVID-19 pandemic. Staff reached out to
  the County of Los Angeles to find out how this bill would be applied and have since found out that in
  July 2020, the County of Los Angeles Board of Supervisors had already granted a twelve month
  extension for all such permits and approvals, including projects in plan check.

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that this does not mean that staff will relax pressure on the
  property owner and applicant to move quickly. Based on discussions with building & safety and the
  property owner, they are very close to permit issuance.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN stated that there will be a Nature Center Community Meeting on
  February 9, 2021 from 5:30 p.m. to 7:00 p.m.

  11.  MANAGER ITEMS

  Planning Manager Naughton stated that a joint City Council, Planning Commission and General Plan
  Advisory Committee meeting will be scheduled to discuss the focus plan in the commercial district
  and the second component to that meeting will be a Housing Element outreach and stakeholder
  meeting. Polling e-mails will be sent later this week.

  A.  COMMITTEE ASSIGNMENTS

  •  Environmental Advisory Committee (2020: Schachter/Yoo)
  •  Equestrian Committee (2020: Zigrang)
  •  Traffic and Safety Committee (2020: Scott)

  The Planning Commissioners had no changes to committee assignments for 2021.

  B.  2021 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING SCHEDULE

  In response to a comment by VICE CHAIR SCOTT, Planning Manager Naughton stated that the July
  5th meeting may be adjourned to a later date due to the Independence Day Holiday.

  12.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, DECEMBER 2, 2020

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, DECEMBER 8, 2020

  C.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, JANUARY 12, 2020 (SPECIAL MEETING)

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEMS 12A THROUGH 12C.

  There being no objection, CHAIR EDLER so ordered.

  13.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR EDLER adjourned the meeting at 7:22 p.m.

  Submitted by,  Approved by,

  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant  Rick Edler, Chair
